prompt: TypeScript cross-instance private access OOP language disallows
answer:
TypeScript’s restriction is caused by its **structural type system**.

In many nominatively typed OOP languages, private members are scoped to the class/type, so a method of `T` can access private members on another `T` instance. TypeScript cannot safely assume that every object structurally matching `T` was created by the class that declared `T` or actually contains that private member.

Therefore, cross-instance private access is disallowed to avoid code calling a nonexistent private member on a structurally compatible object. In TypeScript, `private` members are accessible only within the declaring class. ([search result](https://stackoverflow.com/revisions/4d7e8b94-1109-4a2a-9add-7fe0c49fbd00/view-source))
